title: The Lighthouse on the Rocks
seo_title: Lighthouse Charcuterie Board: Seafood Showpiece & What to Buy
description: A lighthouse charcuterie board for 12 to 15: a striped tower of salami and cheddar rounds on rocks of pumpernickel, with shrimp, smoked salmon and burrata.
hook: A striped lighthouse made of stacked salami and cheese rounds stands on a rocky point, its lantern glowing.

items.name: Cocktail sauce or a pink Marie Rose sauce

why: The tower is a stack of alternating salami and white cheddar rounds on a hidden dowel, which is what lets it stand tall. The red and white stripes come from the food itself.
Around the base, dark pumpernickel makes the rocks, and the sea is shrimp, smoked salmon, burrata, whipped feta and cheese wedges. It's a striking centerpiece for a coastal party or a summer evening.

timeline.what: Slice the salami and cheese rounds and build the tower (keep it wrapped in the fridge). Roast the potatoes and cube the pumpernickel.
Set the tower on its rocky base.
Add the waves, then the beach.
Add the shrimp and salmon from the fridge and light the LED lantern.

faq.q: How does the lighthouse stand up?
faq.a: The salami and cheese rounds are stacked on a food-safe dowel set into a heavy base. The book explains how to build it so it stays steady.
An unsliced salami about 3 inches across. Ask the deli for a whole one.

Cut the rounds and the pumpernickel rocks the day before. Keep the seafood cold until the last minute. Keep meat, cheese and cut fruit out no more than 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F. For a long party, build half, keep the refill in the fridge and top it up halfway through.
